newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: S.Africa's ANC says big names will seek amnesty.
newsitem.headline: S.Africa's ANC says big names will seek amnesty.

text.p: South Africa's ruling African National Congress said on Friday senior members would seek amnesty for actions in the fight against apartheid, but declined to say if President Nelson Mandela was among them.
The Truth and Reconciliation Commission, set up to compile a full picture of the country's 30-year race war, has set May 10 as the deadline for applications for indemnity from prosecution.

"There will be high-profile people applying for amnesty," Mathew Phosa, ANC lawyer and premier of the northeastern Mpumulanga province, told a news conference after talks between party officials and Archbishop Desmond Tutu who heads the commission.
Asked if Mandela himself would apply, Phosa said: "I will not answer that question at this stage."

Mandela was among the ANC leaders who decided in 1961 that the organisation should take up arms in its struggle to end apartheid. He was later sentenced to life imprisonment for treason but was released in 1990 when the process of scrapping apartheid began.
Tutu has said his commission will express an opinion in its final report on whether the ANC is correct in portraying its armed struggle as a "just war".
But he has stressed that the requirement that those on both sides of the struggle apply for amnesty does not necessarily imply moral equality between their actions.
Up to 300 members of the ANC have applied so far for amnesty, including Defence Minister Joe Modise, but Phosa said many more would lodge applications before the deadline.
The party, which made an initial submission to the truth commission last November on its activities during the apartheid years, will present a follow-up report next month.
Phosa said this would include further details of prison camps which the ANC ran in exile, where mutineers and suspected spies were tortured and killed.
The truth commission, whose role is to heal the wounds of apartheid, has so far received a total of 5,500 applications for amnesty, many of them from former members of government security forces.
Neither of the two surviving apartheid-era presidents, P.W. Botha or F.W. de Klerk, has applied.
